narrative_lines: He opens the notepad, uncaps a pen, and writes the date at the top of the page. He looks at it for a moment.
Hal: I'm managing perfectly well. Ask anyone. Ask Dana.
He recovers, and gives a small, practised nod toward the window.
Hal: Forty years of surveys. Most disputes are about where someone thinks the line is.
You offer tea.
Hal: No tea for me. Well, only if it's brewed properly. Pot warmed first.
You bring the tea, and he holds his watch up toward the blank wall.
Hal: Seven minutes fast, you'll notice. Ruth set it. So I'd be on time.
He doesn't seem to hear himself say the name.
You open the book and begin to read. The Bear Who Followed the Map.
1. A heron folds a map into a bear's paw. "For when I am not here." (A tall grey bird at a doorway, a small brown paw closing on paper.)
2. Step one: fish at dawn. The bear sets two bowls on the table. One is eaten. (Two bowls, one full.)
3. Step two: beans planted exactly in rows. The bear is proud. A rabbit waves from the fence. (Perfect rows, a bear standing very straight.)
Hal has stopped writing. The pen is in his hand and the cap is on the table.
Hal: Sensible bear. Follows instructions. Nothing wrong with that.
Hal: Go on. What's the next step?
4. The rabbit brings jam. "Can't stop," says the bear, "I'm following the map." The jam stays on the step. (A jar on a doorstep, a rabbit's ears drooping.)
5. Step seven: the bridge is out. The bear sits at the edge and folds the map smaller. (A gap in a bridge, a bear very small beside it.)
Hal is quiet. He looks at the picture of the bridge.
Hal: Why doesn't the bear ask the rabbit about the bridge?
Hal looks at the bear's two bowls, the picture still open between you.
Hal: I put out two cups every morning. Habit.
A beat.
Hal: I know she isn't coming down.
Hal studies the picture.
Hal: Well. Back to the bridge,
he says, and turns the page for you.
(End of the vertical slice. The rest of the act is not built yet.)
